name: MCM Engineering II, Inc
old_description: For over 25 years we've specialized in building custom made Switchgear
about:
MCM Engineering II, Inc., operating as LS Electric Utah, is based in Enoch, Utah. The company has specialized in custom switchgear manufacturing for more than 25 years, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. It operates as a subsidiary of a larger parent organization, though the parent company is not named in available materials.

The firm designs and builds medium‑voltage metal‑clad and metal‑enclosed switchgear that meets ANSI C37.20.1, C37.20.2, and C37.20.3/4 standards. Its product range covers NEMA 1 and NEMA 3R lineups, paralleling switchgear, substations, integrated power stations, utility metering equipment, severe‑environment enclosures, sheltered‑aisle walk‑ins, power distribution centers, and low‑voltage (480 V) assemblies. All work is performed in‑house through integrated design, fabrication, wiring, and assembly departments, with each project assigned a dedicated project manager and mechanical designer.

Primary customers include electric utilities, industrial plants, and commercial contractors requiring custom power‑distribution solutions. The company cites utility metering gear, substation integration, and paralleling switchgear for generator sets as typical applications.

MCM II emphasizes direct engineering access — bypassing layers of bureaucracy — and a commitment to faster turnaround than industry averages. Its shipping and loading processes are also ISO‑certified, reflecting a focus on quality through final delivery.

name: MDS Manufacturing Llc
old_description: Our modern high-speed liquid silicone molding equipment support press sizes up to 150 tons. We are the only Midwest manufacturer offering these services!
about:
MDS Manufacturing operates from Pacific, Missouri, where it was founded in 2009 as a family-owned business. The company traces its roots back more than 50 years to Marvin D. Skaggs, a plastics industry veteran whose legacy inspired the MDS name. Today, the firm is led by President Dave Skaggs Sr., Vice President Mike Skaggs, Chief Operating Officer Julie Round, Operations Manager Greg Rodermund, and Quality Control Manager Tyler Skaggs.

The shop provides custom plastic injection molding on presses ranging from 85 to 550 tons, liquid silicone rubber (LSR) molding on high-speed equipment up to 150 tons, and injection stretch blow molding (ISBM) to round out a one-stop-shop offering. It also handles assembly and production tooling, with 3-D prototyping samples available to validate designs before committing to mold construction. Mold lead times are quoted at 6–12 weeks depending on complexity and run size.

MDS serves customers across a broad range of industries worldwide, though the company does not list specific sectors on its site. Its capabilities suit any application requiring precision-molded plastic or silicone components, from prototype through production volumes.

The company emphasizes its family-run culture and a “customer-first philosophy” built on collaboration and transparency. It claims to be the only Midwest manufacturer offering high-speed LSR molding up to 150 tons, and it backs that differentiation with decades of hands-on experience passed down from its founder.

about:
MHz Electronics, Inc. is based in Phoenix, Arizona. The company has been buying and selling electronic manufacturing equipment, testing tools, and specialty items for over 35 years. In 1997, it moved to its current 68,000-square-foot facility on East Washington Avenue.

The company operates as a distributor and reseller of electronic components, test equipment, and specialty items. Its inventory exceeds 400,000 parts and equipment, housed in a 68,000-square-foot warehouse that has supported the company’s growth since 1997. MHz Electronics also offers a sourcing service for items not in stock and maintains a want list for customers looking to sell equipment.

The company serves buyers of electronic manufacturing equipment, test instruments, and specialty components across the western United States, with a focus on customers needing hard-to-find or obsolete parts.

MHz Electronics distinguishes itself as the largest in-stock supplier of test equipment in the western United States and emphasizes a sourcing service for hard-to-find items, backed by over three decades of industry experience.

name: MK Fluidic Systems
old_description: MK FLUIDIC SYSTEMS PROVIDES YOU WITH PREMIER FLUIDIC SYSTEM PRODUCTS & COMPONENTS
about:
MK Fluidic Systems was established in 2012 in Las Vegas, Nevada, as a privately owned, family‑operated business. The company traces its roots to founder Mike Kloehn, who spent over 30 years in medical manufacturing helping build the firm his father started in 1970. After that business was sold in 2007, Kloehn saw an opportunity to create a U.S.-based facility focused on premium‑quality, cost‑effective fluidic components for OEMs.

The company designs and manufactures precision syringes, probes, rotary valves, tubing assemblies, sub‑assembly modules, and syringe pumps in its Las Vegas factory. Its capabilities span syringe manufacturing and assembly, fluid‑control valve design and manufacturing, tubing and fitting assembly, probe fabrication, service‑kit kitting, and syringe‑pump production. Prototypes are built on the same production equipment used for volume runs, eliminating a separate transfer step. The firm operates under ISO 13485:2016 and emphasizes a lean, responsive production culture.

MK Fluidic Systems serves OEM customers in the life‑science, diagnostic, analytical, and broader healthcare industries. Its components are integrated into laboratory instruments, clinical analyzers, and analytical systems. The company works directly with OEM development teams to engineer custom liquid‑handling solutions, from initial requirements through validation and full‑scale production.

The business was started to fill a gap for high‑quality, domestically produced fluidic parts at competitive cost. Leadership cites a documented component library that accelerates design, prototyping on production machinery to reduce risk, and a direct customer relationship without intermediaries. Performance metrics reported by the company include 98 % on‑time delivery and 99 % quality‑control acceptance.

name: MN Solar

about:
MN Solar is a solar installation company headquartered in Plymouth, Minnesota. The firm specializes in residential photovoltaic systems and operates under Minnesota electrical contractor license EA758999 and building contractor license BC777439.

The company provides a three-step service process: a free on-site assessment of a home's energy usage and solar potential, full permitting and regulatory compliance handling, and professional installation by a certified crew. MN Solar manages all paperwork and inspections required by local utilities and municipalities, delivering turnkey solar arrays for homeowners.

Its primary customers are residential property owners in Minnesota seeking to reduce electricity costs and hedge against rate increases. Testimonials from clients such as Stephen and Dennis highlight the company's communication and installation quality, with one noting the state electrical inspector's positive comment on workmanship.

MN Solar emphasizes a no-pressure sales approach and transparent communication throughout the project timeline. The company promotes the financial benefits of solar ownership, citing an average 4% increase in home value and long-term savings through incentives like Xcel Energy's Solar*Rewards program.

about:
MRO Electric and Supply operates from Cary, North Carolina, as an independent factory automation distributor. The company has been in business for more than a decade, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names have not been shared.

The company supplies factory-new, surplus, and remanufactured industrial automation components from manufacturers such as Fanuc, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Modicon, Yaskawa, and Control Techniques. It also operates a repair shop that restores CNCs, PLCs, servo and spindle drives, motors, amplifiers, VFDs, and HMIs, typically completing repairs in three to five days. Stock items ship the same day for orders placed before 3 PM Eastern, and all products carry a minimum two-year warranty.

MRO serves industrial automation customers across sectors that depend on motion control and automation systems, including users of CNC machinery, PLC-based production lines, and servo-driven equipment. The company reports over 15,000 satisfied customers but does not disclose specific client names.

The company emphasizes rapid response, promising quotes within 10 minutes during business hours, and highlights its dedicated technician team as a differentiator for diagnosing and repairing servo drives with precision to minimize downtime.

name: MWS Wire Industries
old_description: As a worldwide distributor and manufacturer of magnet and specialty wire, we're empowering what's possible.
about:
MWS Wire Industries is based in Oxnard, California. Founded in 1968 by Al Friedman, the company began in the attic of a garage in Chatsworth, California, driven by customer demand. Friedman, not originally from the wire industry, started small, taking orders by phone and hand-spooling wire, personally delivering to meet deadlines. The business remains family-owned.

The company manufactures and distributes magnet wire and specialty wire, including custom insulated wiring, bare and insulated specialty alloy wire, and proprietary products such as Multifilar®, Twistite®, and Microsquare® magnet wire. Its 75,000-square-foot Oxnard facility comprises 25,000 square feet of manufacturing space and 40,000 square feet of warehouse. Processes include drawing, shaping, spooling, packaging, custom plating (copper, nickel alloys, gold, silver, tin, nickel), twisting, insulating, and serving. The company maintains one of the world’s largest inventories of magnet and specialty wire, enabling same-day shipment for stock items and custom production runs from low minimum quantities to high-volume orders, with custom orders typically completed within four weeks.

MWS serves industries including aerospace (deep-space applications), medical (ultra-fine wire for devices), cryogenic, musical instruments, and electronics. Customers range from large OEMs to product development teams requiring short runs and quick turnarounds.

The company’s founding principle—saying “yes” to customer requests—underpins its reputation for uncompromising service. An in-house ISO-certified testing lab, capable of testing to NEMA MW 1000, and a workforce with decades-long tenure (some over 50 years) support consistent quality and rapid response.

name: Macksteel Warehouse, Inc
old_description: Below are just a few of our capabilities and manufacturing processes that we use to set ourselves apart
about:
Macksteel Warehouse, Inc. is based in Watertown, South Dakota. The company traces its roots to 1973 when Steve and Beverly Mack started a portable baling business processing scrap metals across the region. A few years later they purchased the current property and formed Mack Wrecking, Inc. as a scrap iron and metal recycler. In 1998 the scrap division was sold and the name changed to Macksteel Warehouse, Inc., shifting focus to metal service center operations and adding fabrication equipment to produce finished parts.

Today the company operates nearly 145,000 square feet of space and maintains one of the largest inventories of structural steel in the area, including tube, channel, beam, flat bar, and rod, plus over 5,000 sheets of aluminum, stainless, and carbon steel. Its fabrication capabilities cover metal cutting from 24-gauge up to 3-inch thickness, precision bending driven by modern software, and wire and tube forming. The shop also offers reverse engineering from templates, prints, or scrap parts, and supports product development and prototyping.

Macksteel serves industrial and commercial customers throughout the region who need a combination of raw material supply, custom fabrication, and finished-part manufacturing. The company’s integrated model allows clients to source stock, have it cut and formed, and receive completed assemblies without changing vendors.

The business emphasizes its unified approach — distribution, fabrication, and manufacturing under one roof — as a key differentiator. It also promotes same-day pickup for most orders, a broad in-stock selection, and equipment capable of tight bending tolerances.
